old: Its possible root fuses a word for 'around' with one for 'full' — something bursting on every side.
It traces to the Latin amplus, meaning simply 'large.'
It shares a possible ancestor with 'ambient,' both touching on the idea of surrounding fullness.
clues: A word for having more than enough, it may hide an ancient idea of being full on every side, filled all the way around.
It describes a supply that is generous, more than merely sufficient, or a space that is roomy with room to spare. Its Latin ancestor simply meant 'large.'
It fills the blanks in '___ time to finish the test' and '___ room for everyone.' The 'around' element it may contain also shows up in ambient.
reviewNote: Clue 3's 'plenty of time, or blank time' phrasing was confusing; made the fill-in-the-blank usage clear.
